info.title: DockerCart Store API
info.description:
Customer-facing REST API for the DockerCart storefront: a registered buyer can browse the catalogue, read their own orders and returns, create return requests, and place an order with the same steps as the DockerCart one-page checkout (cart → addresses → shipping quote → payment method → confirm → payment).

**Authentication** — send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or `X-Api-Key: <token>`). Keys are created by the customer in the account area (Account > API) or by an operator in the panel (Customers > edit customer). A key belongs to exactly one customer and can never be used on the admin API (`/api/v1/...`), and vice versa.

**Scopes** — what a key may reach is the intersection of the scopes granted to the customer (group default, overridable per customer) and the scopes stored on the key itself: `products:read`, `orders:read`, `returns:read`, `returns:write`, `checkout:write`. A missing scope is `403 forbidden`.

**Envelope** — successful responses use `{"data": …}` (`meta` on collections). Failures are RFC 9457 problem documents (`application/problem+json`) with `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance` plus the extensions `code`, `request_id` and (on 422) `fields`.

**Dates** — ISO-8601. **Money** — fixed point strings in the store base currency with 4 decimals.

**Text** — free text is stored escaped for the panel and returned as plain text: send the value you want the operator to see (markup is escaped, not interpreted) and expect the same string back on read. Do not pre-encode entities; a `GET → PUT/PATCH` round trip is stable.

**Concurrency** — every single-resource GET returns a strong `ETag`; use `If-None-Match` for cheap 304 polling and `If-Match` on `PUT /v1/addresses/{address_id}`.

**Retries** — every `POST` accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header (8-128 printable characters); repeating the same request with the same key and body replays the stored answer. `POST /v1/checkout/{checkout_id}/confirm` is the one call that creates an order, so always send a key with it.

**Ordering** — the cart is the customer's real cart (the website sees the same lines). A checkout session holds the addresses, the chosen shipping/payment code, the comment and the terms agreement, and reserves stock while it is open; `missing` tells a client what still blocks `confirm`.

**Discovery** — `GET /v1/openapi.json` (no key required) returns this document; the account area renders the same file.

**Payments** — `POST /v1/checkout/{checkout_id}/payment` starts the payment of the confirmed order through the payment method the buyer chose and answers what the client has to do: `kind` is `external` (open `redirect_url` in a browser/WebView), `internal` (a page of this store — nothing to pay online), `html` (render `html`) or `none` (nothing to do; show `instructions`, e.g. cash on delivery). The answer is stored on the checkout and replayed on every repeat, so a retried request never opens a second gateway session; `refresh=1` re-runs it while the order has not moved on.

post.description: Places the order and answers with it (`201`). The session stays readable as `completed` — `GET /v1/checkout/{checkout_id}` still returns its `order_id` — but it can never be confirmed twice (`409 checkout_completed`). Start the payment with `POST /v1/checkout/{checkout_id}/payment`.

post.summary: Start the payment of the confirmed order
post.description:
Runs the payment extension's own execution step for the method chosen at checkout (`payment_code`) and returns what the client has to do next.

`kind`:
- `external` — `redirect_url` points at another host: open it in a browser or WebView (Stripe, PayPal, LiqPay, …).
- `internal` — `redirect_url` is a page of this store only; nothing has to be paid online (the built-in method sends the buyer to the success page).
- `html` — render `html` (an inline form, bank details, …).
- `none` — nothing to do; show `instructions` (cash on delivery, bank transfer, …).

The answer is stored on the checkout and replayed verbatim, so repeating the request is safe — send an `Idempotency-Key` and a lost response can be recovered. `refresh=1` re-runs the module (an expired gateway session) but only while the order status is still the one the previous call left behind; once the payment moved the order on, it answers `409 payment_already_started` instead of charging twice.

The request body is passed through to the module as POSTed fields, for gateways that expect the payment form data in the request.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Language code used for the extension labels (`en-gb`, `ru-ua`, `uk-ua`).

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Re-run the payment module instead of replaying the stored answer (only while the order has not moved on).

schema.description: Optional; forwarded to the payment module's own fields (card data, coupon code, …). The API itself reads nothing from it.
